title: The 5 Longest-Living Animals, Ranked (#1 Is Older Than the Pyramids)

scenes.text: The five longest-living animals on Earth, ranked. Number one was already old when the pyramids were built.

scenes.label: Bowhead whale · 200+ years
scenes.text: Number five: the bowhead whale. Over two hundred years. Whalers have found century-old harpoon tips still in them.

scenes.label: Greenland shark · 400 years
scenes.text: Number four: the Greenland shark. Around four hundred years. It isn't even an adult until one hundred and fifty.

scenes.label: Ocean quahog · 507 years
scenes.text: Number three: an ocean quahog clam named Ming. Five hundred and seven years, counted in the rings of its shell.

scenes.label: Black coral · 4,265 years
scenes.text: Number two: black coral off Hawaii. Four thousand two hundred and sixty-five years old, and still growing.

scenes.label: Glass sponge · 11,000 years
scenes.text: Number one: a glass sponge in the East China Sea. About eleven thousand years old. It was alive before farming existed.

description:
The five longest-living animals, ranked by the oldest verified individual.
A whale over 200, a shark near 400, a clam at 507, a coral past 4,000 — and a sponge that has been alive for about 11,000 years.
Would you want to live that long?
first_comment: Would you take 11,000 years as a sponge, or 80 as a human? Which should we rank next?
